en: The Compendium of Practice (Caryāsaṃgraha) (1) 1. (NC. 23 no.
song) Oṃ, homage to Śrī Cakrasaṃvara! Oṃ, homage to Śrī Vajravārāhī! The melody of the throat-jewel, sung with the devotion of a disciple: Ahedi (Āheri).
O Tāla! O Mātha! O Hāḍābharaṇa! Perform the ritual action; repeatedly assuming self-restraint, O Kapālin! O Veśa!
You Maṇḍikas, you who dwell in cemeteries,
with disheveled hair and naked as the sky.
[Chorus: O, O, O! My King Saṃvara, take Sundarī, the beauty of the battlefield!
O Vajravārāhī, we who have strayed from the path, destroy— yes, shatter—
the cage of our bodies!
He feeds śāli rice with meat and sweets; camphor becomes his betel-leaf, its color like the blue of the sky.
I bow to the yogīs who have merged into the sphere of Meru and are absorbed in existence.
(2) Triyam ṣaḍaṣaṭ hūṃ chādigora (one should abandon) the vow; pa-irā-i, the Lord Śūnya, who is separated from me.
O Vajravārāhī,
without you, I see only darkness.

O Vajravārāhī, who dwells within the mandala of the bliss of the samaya, having propitiated your feet with hundreds of oblations, may you blaze forth from the heart of the playful vajra that pervades all things!
2. (NC. 33 no. song) Rāga: Vibhāsa; Tāla: Omit (NC. & NP. read mātha).
Hold, hold the earth, O Supporter of the Earth! Hold, hold it upon the head of the Cakra! O Crusher, O Crusher, O Wielder of the Vajra, O Samaya Kunduru, O Yogin, O Hero, O Best of Heroes!
Kuru kuru, O Vajradhara! You are the commitment (*samaya*). Perform the *ālolikā* at Karṇavola (Karṇavara)!
O you who wear earrings, O earring! You who bear the body, you who possess the *susamākā* (the *suṣumnā*);
you who hold the lotus of the mind!
Vajra, Śūrya, Ājñāna, Tama.
Thus, at all times, I am the great Ratnākara, possessing the strength of the excellent Vajra-mountain, wearing a necklace of thorny garlands upon my neck.
It is eternal, yet devoid of intrinsic nature; it is supremely eternal, possessing the innate nature (*sahaja-svabhāva*). This is the time of the Jina, the supreme illuminator that binds the body.
HŪṂ HRĪṂ (HĪṂ) Pragñādhṛk! O you adorned with the girdle of the pledge (samayamekhala), in the bliss of Praṇava,
HŪṂ PHAṬ ĀDILA!
I bow at the feet of the excellent one, by the words of Śūratavajra (the supreme song of Śūratavajra).
(4) 3. (NC. does not include this song) Rāga:
[omits *ekatāla*] Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Lord of the Lotus Dance! (*oṃ namo śrīpadmanṛtyeśvarāya*)
Oṃ, homage to Śrī Cakrasaṃvara!
Bhase, the universe, the cosmic egg!
O Lord of the Sun and Moon, you who seize the fragments [of existence],
you who possess the peak of the Amarū mountain, you who cause the wheel of the Bhrāmeḍī to revolve.
O Lord of Mountains, O Vṛndāvana, O Moon, may you wipe away the fierce darkness of this world, which is subject to the insults of primordial nature.

May the graceful ocean-like [dance] of the Lord Padmanṛtyeśvara, performed in the manner of the *tāṇḍava*, with hands [brandishing weapons], be for protection against the fall of calamity (*kṣatrapāta*). May it be so.
Moreover, the snares of the mind construct the wheel of saṃsāra; yet through the grace of that which is accomplished by the Great Cause, they are rendered white with serenity.

Having dispelled doubt regarding one’s own true nature by the Master, and having realized that [nature], one should abandon the web of conceptual constructions regarding happiness; thus, one should always, at all times, bow with humility to the lotus-feet of that Lord, the hundred-fold Guru.
(5) 4. (NC. does not include this song) Rāga: Tāla omits NP. mentioned rāga.
Andhārabhairavī (Gandhārabhairavī):
Oṃ, homage to the glorious Padmanṛtyeśvara!
Oṃ, homage to Śrī Cakrasaṃvara!
The Dharmadhātu is the heart of the Jinas; she is Ānandakālīkā (Kālikā).
His eyes are the light of the world.
Seated upon a lotus throne, they possess the luster of the moon and are free from blemish.
Those whose hearts are the totality of the Victors, beautiful with splendor, are of the nature of innate bliss.
Mañjukumāra dances.
5. (NC. 34 no. song) Rāga: Andhāri (Gandhāri) [NC. & NP mention Gandhārabhairavi]; Tāla:
[Omitting NC. & NP., which mention *cappali*: O Viśvasaroruha, whose face is pervaded by the moon-like orb of the syllable *oṃ*, you are well-born (*susambhavā*).
I bow, I bow to Vāgīśvara, the lord of speech,
who dwells in the hearts of all sages.
O you who lie upon the serpent, charming with the playful grace of the celestial palace, possessing all [perfections].
O Heart of the Victors!
Yellow, blue, and red, with three faces white, yellow, and red, adorned with a crown of five Jinas and jewels.
I shall proclaim the supreme primordial Vajra, the jewel of the Victor’s qualities, whose excellent feet are bowed to by gods and asuras.
6. (NC. 62 no. song) Rāga:
Gandhārabhairavī; Tāla: Jhāpa Harasira (Haraśira).
They scatter crowns, radiant with jewels, at his pair of feet. (7) Dhruva.
To my own Vajrasattva, the Supreme Lord, the Ultimate State.
The Gāndhārī-sun has drunk deeply from the throat of the body-bearer of Vikaṇṭha; it flows, vibrating, and is restrained at the secret throat by the pen of the Yuga.
7. (NC. 5 no. song) Rāga: Bhairavī; Tāla: (NP.
reads *sani*) O Earth! O Meru! O Ocean! O people, wealth, and the forest of the dull-witted (*jaḍavana*).
Like the moon reflected in water.
The eyes, like lotuses, bloom day after day upon the face.
Having taken up the qualities of the Jina in jest,
he bears them upon his neck (or shoulders); though all sense objects are like the waves of a single ocean, the Jina is both one and many.
The wind, having split the two firm and stable vessels,
causes the funeral pyre to blaze.
The Vajra-fire burns here and there [in the ten directions].
Having meditated upon the Sugata-jewel, one bathes;
having recited "Svadhā Suratavajra," there is inconceivable abiding in enlightenment.
8. (NC. 54 no. song) Rāga:
Gandhārabhairavī; Tāla: Jhāpa; Subject: Tribhuvana (the three worlds).
The radiant Muralīdhara [is] the one who disciplines Vinayavatī. (9) Refrain.
O Vajrasattva, supreme lord, do not remain hidden within the forest.
Possessing ten thousand rays like a thousand suns, manifesting in many kinds of forms, and through his passion for the sun and moon, he delights in those endowed with sentient beings.
9. (NC. does not include this song) Rāga: Bhairavī, Ekātāla. The Lord of the Earth, Śiriṣa, was born at an untimely hour.
The tree-dwelling Bhairavas,
the father Vradhmapati, and the serpent Vasuki are fierce, formidable, and terrifying.
The clouds are whirling.
Dhru.
Oṃ! Gaṇapati, Kumāra, Mahākāra (Mahākāla),
Kṣetrapāla, and the hosts of Yoginīs, accept these fivefold offerings of liquor, meat, and fish.
Eat and drink, indeed!
To the one born from the *ka*-group, who possesses the sound of thunder, the giver of wealth, the *pippala* tree,
the fierce Bhairava, and the consort of Rudra (*Rudrāṇī*).
The white Takṣaka nāgas, the Gaṇadharas, the deep [thundering] clouds, and the cremation grounds.

In the monastery born from the *ca*-group, there is Varuṇa; [there dwell] the Aśvaka tree, Ruruka, Bhairava, Indrāyaṇī, Kuṅkuma, Kakkoṭaka (Karkaṭaka), the Nāgas, and clouds roaring with masses of flames.

(10) In the group beginning with *ṭa*, which resembles a mountain, there is the *cūta* tree; Kapila Bhairava, Vārāhī, the red lotus, the serpent (*bhujaṅga*), Kuruka Bhairava, and the clouds of movement.
When the *tavarga* arises, there are a single tree and its peak; the Karaṅga tree, Krodhabhairava, Kaumāri, Raktā, Mahāpadmanāga, Aḍhūtahāsā, Pracaṇḍa, and Jaladā.
In the *pavarga* group, from the *mātṛgṛha*, there arise the tree Pakkoṭi, Unmattabhairava, Vaiṣṇavī, Śyāmā, Anantanāga, Lakṣmīvana, Hūtāsana, and Puruṣajalada.
In the class of the *ya*-varga, there is the void (*śūnya*),
the wind of the house, the *arjuna* tree, Saṃhārabhairava, Cāmuṇḍā who is red, the Kulika serpent, and the terrible darkness (*ghorāndhakāra*).
The clouds that provide sustenance.
In the forest born of the *śa* class [of consonants], in the northeast, there is the *vartaka* tree;
the terrifying and fearsome Mahālakṣmī, Śvetā, the serpent Śaṅkhapāla, and the clouds raining down *kilikili-lāva*.
I bow to Śrī Heruka, who removes the fear of cyclic existence, whose feet are embraced by Kāmodā, Bhairavakālī, and Bharaṇī; who has twelve eyes, four faces, and a face like the rays of the sun.
10. (NC. does not include this song) Rāga: Kāmoda O Khadakaṅkāla, O Lord of the Three Triads, perform your ritual! O Lord of Śacī, go to your own abode; do not remain here.
The net of dog-like hair is now being shaken off; like dust, the activity of the senses is being swept away.
O Lord of the World, may your pride and anger remain; let them perform the act of cutting [the bonds].
I am the king of the Puṇyajanas; I am the compassionate Lord of the North. May you behold me with smiles like the moon at dawn.
May the lords of the wide path flee at once; this is the binding with the vajra-noose that effects their slaughter.
When the world, including air, fire, and earth, has perished, I alone remain; there is no fault in this.
O King of the hosts of yakṣas, go to Laṅkāpuri; O Lord Heruva, carry out the command of binding.
O Rudra-Gaṇeśvara, O creator of obstacles for men, may you fulfill and uphold the command of the Lord Śaktinātha.
Then, in the upper half of the world, Brahmā [is visualized] with a sword for his sky-like thought, holding ashes as if vomiting them out.
I am the wrathful one named Buddhavarana; dwelling in the ten directions, I bring terror to Mara.
O Vācchali, hold my feet in your hands; sing the verses that possess the splendor of a thunderbolt.
11. (NC. does not include this song) Rāga: Bhairavī Jhāpa Oṃ khavajra kuvajra hūṃkāre kāri (kāli)
O enemy, bend your bow at night!
Immediately after shattering [them], O Great Wrathful One, speak and drive away the multitude of obstacles!
(12) Gha gha! Strike, strike! O you who destroy all that is wicked, nail them down! Hūṃ phaṭ! O you who remove sin!
Oṃ! Vajra stake! O Vajradhara, by your command, you stake the body, speech, and mind!
Having propitiated Śrī Vajrasattva, who bestows the supreme siddhi and grants the fruit of liberation.
At the eastern gate is Kākānana,
who possesses the luster of a shattered person and a terrible form.
O fierce, terrifying, and formidable great charnel grounds, you who are the hosts of the lords of gods, you dance!
At the gate of the northern direction, O Owl-faced One,
you are dark-complexioned with terrifying eyes.
O Lord of Yakṣas, you who dwell in the cremation grounds with a fierce form, you pierce the sky.
At the western gate of the cremation ground, there is a Siddhu of reddish-brown body and fierce form.
O hosts of lords of spirits, you play in the great cremation ground filled with flames!
O you with the face of a boar at the gate of the southern direction, whose body is like molten gold and who rings out the sound of a bell!
O hosts of the Lord of Pretas in the great cremation ground, terrifying with its dark spots, you pierce [them] through!
In the southern corner, O Goddess,
is Yamadādi, who has a dark-yellow luster and a fierce form.
O great cremation ground of unrestrained laughter, the hosts of Tejādhipati play there!
In the second corner is Yamadyuti, with a body like a father-sun, red in color and of wrathful form.
O great cremation ground of Lakṣmīvana, you who are the seat of Hūtaśana, you cause the hosts of the lords of the Rākṣasas to dwell here!
In the northwest corner (the excellent corner of the god Vāyu),
O Goddess Yamadraṃṣṭrī.
Reddish-brown in complexion, with a dark body and a terrifying face.
In the terrifying,
fearsome great cremation ground, O Goddess, the hosts of Vātādhipati play in the excellent northeast corner.
Yamamathanī,
who is yellowish-black in luster and possesses a terrifying form.
In the great cremation ground, the hosts of Bhūtas and Ādhipatis raise a fierce *kilikilā* cry and play their instruments.
The Uṣṇīṣacakravartin is situated above, removing the obstacles of Māra,
with a yellow body.
The hosts of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, along with the gods, sages, and celestial beings, are struck down.
The wrathful Sumbharāja, with an exceedingly dark-blue form, is the destroyer of the Māras dwelling in the netherworld (pātāla).
The hosts of asuras, Śeṣanāga, and others pierce the earth and the multitude of beings that move upon it.
O HŪṂ-syllable that burns the body and the ten directions, I prostrate to you, O Ten Great Wrathful Ones!
O Lord of Generosity who fulfills all hopes! O you who have warded off the obstacles of Māra!
(13) 12. (NC. 24 no. song) Rāga: Kāmoda.
His body has the luster of a sapphire; his form arises from the blazing *hūṃ* syllable, [appearing as] Khaḍakāṅkāla.
The creator of the emanation of all that exists, wearing a jewel crown, the Lord of Wrath.
Dhru.

I bow to the illustrious Pracandavira, the destroyer of the elephant of worldly existence, the Lord of the Universe who pervades the three worlds, and the one who brings about the destruction of the enemies of the Vedas.

He stands with infinite valor, a hero of the three worlds; in his right hand he holds aloft a sharp sword, and with his left thumb he grasps a noose at his heart, terrifying and binding the enemies of worldly existence.
Her body adorned with various jewel necklaces,
anklets,
and girdles, she is terrifying to behold.
She whose terrifying face is the conflagration of the three worlds is the fierce heroine.

The remover of all fears for the lord of heroes, the pacifier of pretas, piśācas, and the like, he whose feet are worshipped by gods and men with their minds, and who bestows the fruits of all accomplishments and liberation.
13. (NC. does not include this song) Rāga: Hoṇḍāra (Hindola); Tāla: Mātha; Hūṃkāra has arisen, equal to sapphire (indranīlasama).
His body was radiant with splendor, blazing with flames, and entirely enveloped in a mass of fire.
(14) Firm.
Victory to the immovable one who possesses manifold forms and holds a sword and a noose in his hands!
O Lord of the World, O Protector of the World, Great King of Wrath!
With her left knee placed upon the earth, possessing a fierce countenance and three eyes, she who is the owl-eyed Rākṣasa, the terrifier of worldly existence, and the destroyer of all obstacles.
O Brahmā-Hari-Hara, you who burn away pride through the central channel, O auspicious hero (Suvīra),
you who crush the earth with your gaze, you whose rays are immediate, the destroyer of obstacles!
Adorned with various jewel ornaments, wearing a divine crest-jewel (*mauli*) of precious gems,
it bestows the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of all desired wealth for the world.
14. (NC. 47 no. song) Rāga: Madhumatī; Tāla: Durjambha; [The one] who has delighted the twelve [suns].
O Vajravārāhī, who resides in a celestial mansion situated upon the Meru-maṇḍala like the beautiful earth, adorned with twelve arms and four faces, and embracing [the Lord] by the neck!
Dhrū. ||
Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Burning [the ten directions], radiating, all Māras, O Awakening! Embrace the pairs in the non-dual nature.
Thus it was said regarding the gift of Śrī Samvaralāyā.

She is beautifully adorned with a vajra, a bell, an elephant hide, a trident, a curved knife, and a hand-drum; she holds a skull-cup filled with marrow, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a noose, an axe, and the Brahma-head.

Adorned with the crown of the five supreme Victors, embellished with the ornaments of the six mudrās, embracing the vowels and consonants, holding a bow, clothed in a tiger skin, and possessing a black body.

Adorned with a garland of human heads and skulls, the glorious Saṃvara possesses divine vision and a compassionate heart; he is the refuge for those who seek the means to cross the desert of birth after birth. Thus sings the supreme primordial Vajra.
15. (NC. 57 no. song) Rāga: Bhairavī;
Jhāpa in the middle; Merumahāmaṇi; adorned with a crown of golden rays (or: adorned with golden rays).
In the worlds of Pūrvavideha, Jambūdvīpa, Aparagodānīya, and Uttarakuru, the five Victors pervade with their five colors.
Dhrū. ||
Homage to the five Buddhas: the creator of the universe, the benefactor of the universe,
the nectar of the universe, the fivefold power, and the fire of the eight continents.
May those whose minds are victorious over the world carry away the dense, terrible darkness of both kinds of ignorance.
Jātavedanasya-yā-upadīpa (Upadvīpa),
Ro-upadvīpa (Raupadvīpa),
Rijātudhyāne-svasana-rā-upadvīpa (Raupadvīpa).
And he enjoys the fourfold [offerings] in the world,
O Śrīkhaṇḍaparaśu, on the subcontinent.

(16) Having drunk the blood of men from the eastern direction, licking the seven and eight petals, O fair one, they have discharged their arrows and discs, making all the treasures of the serpent race known.

The excellent Guru’s triple vow— that devotion, that meditation, the worship with the flower of the mind and the water of purity, and the recitation of the *praṇava*— adorned by these seven, becomes a bridge for crossing the ocean of existence.
16. (NC. 16 no. song) Rāga:
Paṭamañjarī;
Tāla: Mātha; Anila, Anala.
In the midst of the world of Jalajodbhava is the circle of gurus, the sovereign of the wheel,
the vajra-penetrating cage.
The Lord of the Great Mandala Circle, who completely shatters the entire web of existence.
Dhrū. ||
The sound of the hand-drum (*ḍamaru*) is the play of emptiness and compassion; the embrace is the play of the syllables of Heruka;
[the sound] is Vajravārāhī.
The emission of the syllables of the embrace (the play).
O Lord of the Thirty-six Heroes, gather [them] there in each of those eight cremation grounds;
O Unstruck One,
[you who are] all the gods (or the corpse of the gods).
The sixteen goddesses of the Vajra [family] abide in the intrinsic nature of both.
The three worlds are your single bed; the three worlds are your one heroic display. The nine dramas of the three worlds unfold within the expanse of the cosmic egg.
Both have the same aspect (or one aspect).
Day and night, may they abandon attachment; may they cast off worldly existence and non-existence, and may they cast off the bonds of fear regarding birth and death.
The state of fearlessness (or victory) is by nature beyond comparison.
17. (NC. 80 no. song) Rāga: Lalita; Tāla:
Jhāpa Anuttara (Supreme).

The syllable *tathatā* (or *evaṃ*) within its own nature (*svabhāve*), a variegated vase adorned with the form of jewels, filled with the water of vajra-amṛta consecrated seven times by the syllables *oṃ āḥ hūṃ*, consisting of the clay of primordial wisdom.

(18) The essence of fierce nectar (the moon-nectar), bestower of the fruit of enlightenment, pervaded by all the Victors, the innate vase that purifies the impurities of the world, the state of emptiness and compassion, the destroyer of cyclic existence, whose form is free from letters.

The five nectars, joined with fragrant water (*gandhāmbu*), are placed within a conch shell; empowered by the *hūṃ* mantra and consecrated with flowers, this vessel of the *vipātra* is established as the vajra.
Having drawn forth the state of molten form within the jar,
[one should] instantly bring the water-form of the Mandākinī and the common circle of deities, headed by Jñānasattva, into the heart-vajra-jar.

The water for the feet and so forth, the merit of offering the water for sipping, and the stainless flask entered by the commitment being (samayasattva) melt into the great passion, taking the form of the awakening mind (bodhicitta); thus, the commitment being and the wisdom being (jñānasattva) become one.
18. (NC. 29 no. song) Rāga:
Gandhārabhairavī; Tāla: Jhāpa Trini (Tini).
And perform the four divine abodes (brahmavihāras) with the *loyana* (locana) mantra during the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*) and the maṇḍala fire-offering (*homa*).
Dhrū. ||
Having performed the *homa* at home, [recite] "Hūṃ Hūṃ. Abandon, abandon the bonds of passion, hatred, and delusion, O young maiden! (Abandon them!)
O Vajra, Prajñā is the bell and Upāya is the sun and moon; O Ācārya, [this] is the bow. (Va-iṭhā)
(19) Holding a *śruva* ladle in the left hand and a vessel of wine (*surā*) in the right, he offered oblations into the blazing fire of the vajra.
O Karṇa, at the outer edge,
within the inner homa, you are fully awakened by the thunderous wind and dense clouds.
19. (NC. 59 no. song) Rāga: Nāṭa; Tāla: Jaṭi. Red-colored, with three eyes.
O beautiful one, you who possess eighteen arms and weapons that radiate light!
Dhrū. ||
O Goddess Vāruṇī,
O Goddess Māmakī!
O delighter of the world, O charming one of divine passion!
In the Āgamas, Vedas, and Purāṇas, as well as in the exposition of the path of Yoga, initiation, and the instructions of the Guru;
O you who are the very embodiment of the five Buddhas, may Heruka be present within Heruka among all these yoginīs.
Having attained the skill of the feet of the hundred gurus,
he who is firm in his realization speaks as Vāg-vajra, the embodiment of the divine swan.
(20) 20. (NC. 36 no. song) Rāga: Bhairavī; Tāla: Trihūrā (NP. trihulā).
Homage! O you who bear the form of the syllable *A*, O pure being, you who wear the *ūrṇā* hair-tuft!
Dhru.
Therefore, huṃ huṃ; therefore, tete huṃ huṃ huṃ.
He is in union with his consort through the yoga of embracing, and he holds the vajra and bell mudrās.
He who bears a body white as a conch shell, pure like the autumnal moon.
The world is absorbed in the body of illusion; may I [attain] compassion and strength.
21. (NC. 81 no. song) Melody: Śṛṅgāramāraśrī;
Rhythm: Mātha. In the midst of the solar and lunar mandalas, Anandamudrā stands embracing Vajravārāhī and Samvara; she is intensely radiant with manifold rays of light.
tenā hūṃ hūṃ tenā hūṃ hūṃ tenā tete hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ ||
Blue in color, with four faces (four-faced),
three eyes on each face, possessing a form of supreme bliss, she bears the Viśvavajra and the crescent moon upon her matted hair-turban, and is beautifully adorned with ornaments of human bone.

Holding a vajra-bell, elephant-hide, hand-drum, and khaṭvāṅga, she bestows the bliss of cessation; she carries a skull-cup, axe, noose, trident, and the head of Brahmā, and her waist is encircled by a tiger-skin skirt.

I bow, I bow to the goddess Yamaḍākinī, who has the face of a crow and so forth, whose form is innate bliss, and who dwells upon the earth; she is Śrī Cakrasaṃvara, propitiated at the feet of the hundred gurus.
22. (NC. 60 no. song) Rāga: Pañcama; Tāla: Jhāpa. Jvalita Vajranara (Vajrānala).
When the sun and moon are drawn together in the *kunduru-yoga* in the form of the sound of *oṃkāra*, the three worlds are dissolved.
The Jina is the moon, whose form is the bindu.
Dhrū. ||
O Śrī Mañjuśrīvajra, the Lord of Wrath who assumes a form of supreme bliss! Oṃ Āḥ! (22)
Hūṃ! O glorious Mañjuvajra, Lord of the Wrathful Ones!
Through the union of the vajra and the lotus, the innate bliss arises; O Wind-Wave,
O Three-Faced One, O Six-Armed One, lead us across the three realms.
Wearing a jewel crown, black in color with a white face, [holding] in the right and left [hands].
Seated upon a moon-disc and a double-vajra cross-legged posture (*vajraparyaṅka*),
his body blazing like saffron, he holds in his right hands a vajra, a sword, and an arrow, and in his left hands a bell, a lotus, and a bow.
Adorned with various jewel ornaments, he radiates many forms, a hundredfold venerable.
By the grace of your lotus feet, I bow down and prostrate myself at your playful abode.
23. (NC. 40, no. song) Rāga:
Dhanāśrī;
Tāla: Jaṭi. The Great Bliss, which is both imperishable and fourfold bliss, pervades the body and radiates throughout the three worlds.
The King of Great Bliss has split the two drums of the moon and the sun—this is the refrain.
Neither attached to evil nor attached to merit,
possessing the singular nature of the three worlds, he is the destroyer of all conceptual constructions.
The goddess, the bestower of the boon of unsurpassed gnosis,
dwells within the circle of Amitābha; she assumes a human-like form for the duration of an eon and holds a skull-cup.

Bearer of the *khaṭvāṅga*, possessing the body of the boon-granting wisdom-knowledge (*prajñājñāna*), naked, wearing a crown and hair-locks, adorned with a discus, earrings, a necklace, a breast-ornament, a girdle, and anklets; bearing a garland of Rudra-skulls and human bones— the Goddess who is the mother of all Tathāgatas, free from existence and non-existence.
Śrī Vajrayoginī’s feet rest upon my head;
